title: How to play a slideshow on a second display in Keynote on Mac: step by step
metaTitle: Play Keynote Slideshow on Second Display on Mac: Steps
description: How to play a slideshow on a second display in Keynote on Mac: turn off mirroring, choose Play > In Fullscreen, then click Play.
targetKeyword: how to play a slideshow on a second display in keynote on mac
secondaryKeywords: present Keynote on an external monitor
intro: To play a Keynote slideshow on a second display on a Mac, turn off mirroring in System Settings > Displays, choose Play > In Fullscreen, then click the Play button in the toolbar. The slideshow goes to the external display, and the presenter display stays on your Mac.
tldr: Turn off mirroring in System Settings > Displays so the external screen can show its own picture.
Choose Play > In Fullscreen, then click the Play button in the toolbar.
The audience sees the slide on the external display. You see the presenter display on your Mac.
Press X to swap the two screens if they are on the wrong sides.
Keynote for iCloud in a browser follows a different path, covered in its own section below.

blocks.text: A second display can go wrong in three quiet ways. The screen stays on the desktop, the slideshow lands on the wrong screen, or the presenter view never appears. Most of the time the cause is mirroring, where the second display copies your Mac screen instead of extending it. The steps below fix all three, and the sections after them explain what each screen should show.
Before you start: what you need

You need Keynote for Mac 15.4 or later, which requires macOS 26 or later according to Apple. Check your version by opening Keynote and choosing Keynote > About Keynote. The presenter display is older than that. Apple says it arrived in Keynote 11.0 as a separate presenter window with notes, the current slide, and the next slide.

items: A cable or adapter that matches your display's input, tested with your Mac before the day
A display that is switched on and detected by macOS before you open the presentation
A spare cable or adapter in your bag, in case the first one fails
A remote or a keyboard in reach, if you advance slides from across the room

blocks.text: Turn off mirroring before you play

Mirroring sends the same picture to both screens. When mirroring is on, there is no separate screen for the presenter display to use. Apple's Keynote for iCloud page makes the same point: without this setting, viewers may see the presenter window. Treat mirroring as the first thing to check, even when the slideshow itself looks fine.

A quick test tells you whether mirroring is on. Look at both screens. If they show the same desktop picture and the same windows, mirroring is on. If the external display shows a different picture or an empty desktop, the displays are extended and you are ready to play. The arrangement lives in System Settings, not in Keynote, so change it there and then return to your presentation.
What shows on each screen

When the slideshow runs in full screen on an external display, Keynote splits the work. The audience display shows only the slide. Your Mac shows the presenter display, which gives you the current slide, the next slide, your notes, and a timer. With more connected displays, the presenter display can also appear on those screens.

blocks.caption: Default layout when you play In Fullscreen on an external display.

blocks.text: If the layout is backward, press X. Keynote swaps the two screens without touching your slides or your notes. It is faster than dragging windows around, and it does not change the order of the slides.
Change what the presenter display shows

Move the pointer anywhere on the presenter display, then click a button at the top to show the toolbar. Display Configuration sits at the top right. From there you show or hide each part of the presenter view. Apple also lists a Use Auto Layout option under Customize Presenter Display.

items: Current Slide
Next Slide
Presenter Notes
Ready to Advance Indicator
Clock
Timer

blocks.text: Hide the Next Slide if the view feels busy. Keep Presenter Notes on if you read from a script. Keep the Timer on if you need to finish on time. Test each combination during a rehearsal, so the screen fits how you talk.

If you have not written speaker notes yet, the [presenter notes guide](/how-to/add-presenter-notes-in-keynote) shows how to add them. Notes you write there appear in the presenter view when Presenter Notes is on.
Keynote for iCloud on a second display

Keynote for iCloud runs in a browser, and the path is different from the Mac app. Apple's steps start with the Play button in the toolbar. You then open the presenter display from the bottom of the slideshow, move the slideshow window, and go full screen. Follow this order.

items: Click Play in the toolbar.
Move the pointer to the bottom center of the slideshow and click Open Presenter Display.
Drag the slideshow window to the connected display.
Click Full Screen in the bottom-center controls.
Press ? or click Presentation Shortcuts at the top right of the presenter display to see the keys.

blocks.text: Apple's iCloud page also says to turn mirroring off first, under System Settings > Displays > Arrangement. On Windows, the equivalent is the Extend desktop setting. Apple does not list a browser requirement on that page, so check the iCloud help if one browser behaves differently.
Play in a window instead of full screen

Choose Play > In Window when you need the Mac desktop visible, for example to switch to a demo or a video. The Play menu then offers Show Presenter Display in Window and Hide Presenter Display in Window. You can also use the Show Presenter Display button at the top of the slideshow window.

Use In Full Screen for the talk itself, and In Window for rehearsals or quick checks on your Mac. Switch modes between runs, not in the middle of your talk. A window that moves unexpectedly is harder to recover from on stage.
Fix a presenter display that does not show

One Apple Community thread describes a laptop screen that went black in full screen over HDMI, on macOS 13.5. The top reply suggested a checkbox under Keynote > Preferences > Slideshow, labeled Enable Presenter Display in full screen. Apple staff did not reply, and the thread is closed. Treat that reply as a user suggestion, not an Apple instruction.

Apple's current list for Keynote > Settings > Slideshow includes Show pointer when using the mouse or trackpad, Show slideshow controls when pointer is at the bottom of the screen, and Show presenter display in other applications. It does not list a Presenter Display toggle for the full screen case. That checkbox could not be confirmed in the current app, so do not count on it.

If your Mac screen goes black in full screen, try Play > In Window as a fallback. Then test with the exact cable and adapter you will carry on the day. A setup that works at your desk can still fail on a different adapter.
Projector and TV setups

Projectors and TVs often run at a different resolution than your Mac screen. Check the display settings in System Settings > Displays if the slide looks cropped or blurry. Pick the resolution the display recommends when you can. A slide that looks sharp in the editor should look the same in full screen, so test with the real screen before the talk.
Keyboard keys for running the show
Apple's Mac guide names keys in words rather than with symbols, so this page does not give ⌘, ⌥, ⌃, or ⇧ combinations. The keys below are the ones Apple documents for playback.

items: Space bar or Right Arrow: advance to the next slide
Left Arrow: go back or reset a build
A number, then Return: jump to that slide
X: swap the slideshow and the presenter display
Esc: stop the slideshow

blocks.text: Practice the number jump at home. It is easy to type the wrong number under pressure, and a wrong slide in front of an audience is hard to hide.
Keynote version and macOS requirements
Version numbers matter here because the presenter display has changed over the years. Apple's What's New page gives the history in short form. Use this list to see which version added each change.

items: 11.0: a separate presenter window with notes, current slide, and next slide
11.2: slideshow controls, keyboard shortcuts, and multi-presenter controls
14.1: control over where the presenter display appears when rehearsing with multiple displays
15.4 for Mac: requires macOS 26 or later

blocks.text: The 15.4 changes add Creator Studio themes, beta intelligent slide generation, request access to collaborate, and Siri questions about Keynote. None of them change the second display steps on this page.
Is Keynote free for this?

Yes. Apple says Keynote remains free for all users and comes included with new Mac purchases. Keynote 15.1 joined Apple Creator Studio, but creating, viewing, editing, and real-time collaboration do not need a subscription.

Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year in the U.S., with a one-month free trial for new subscribers. It adds premium templates, themes, Content Hub, and beta intelligence features. Nothing in the second display steps needs it. Check Apple's newsroom for current pricing before you subscribe.
Mistakes people make on the day

The most common mistake is testing on the built-in screen only. Everything works there, then the projector shows the desktop. Test with the external display connected, using the same cable you will bring to the event.

The second mistake is starting from the wrong slide. The slideshow begins on the slide you select, so click the right one before you choose Play. The third is forgetting that Presenter Notes can be off. A blank presenter view looks broken, but it is only a toggle.
Rehearse the setup before the talk

Rehearse in the same room, with the same display and cable, if you can. Choose Play > In Fullscreen, check the presenter display, then press X once to see what changes. Press X again to return the layout you want.

Apple added control over where the presenter display appears when rehearsing with multiple displays in Keynote 14.1. If you use more than one extra screen, check that control before the event, not during it.
Next steps after the slideshow works

If you want a backup in case the display fails, export the deck as a movie. The guide [How to export a Keynote presentation as a movie on Mac](/how-to/export-a-presentation-as-a-movie-in-keynote) covers that. If you teach, the [Keynote for teachers page](/for/teachers/keynote) covers lesson slides and presenter view.

If you want to write notes by voice, the [dictation guide for Keynote speaker notes](/blog/dictate-in-keynote-mac-speaker-notes) shows the steps. Set dictation up before the rehearsal, not on the morning of the talk.

If the presenter display still will not appear, gather your macOS version, Keynote version, cable type, and mirroring setting. Apple Support and the Keynote community forums are good places to ask, and those details make an answer much faster.

faq.question: Why does my second display show the desktop instead of the slideshow?
faq.answer: The slideshow only moves to the second display when you play it in full screen. If the displays are mirrored, the second screen copies your Mac, so turn mirroring off first. Then choose Play > In Fullscreen and click Play again.

faq.question: Can the presenter display stay on my Mac while the slideshow runs on a projector?
faq.answer: Yes. That is the default. The slideshow goes to the external display, and the presenter display stays on your Mac. If the projector is on the wrong side, press X to swap them.

faq.question: Do I need a subscription to present on a second display?
faq.answer: No. Keynote is free, and Apple says creating, viewing, editing, and real-time collaboration do not need a subscription. Apple Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year in the U.S. and adds premium themes and beta intelligence features.

faq.question: Which macOS version do I need for Keynote 15.4?
faq.answer: Keynote 15.4 for Mac requires macOS 26 or later, according to Apple's What's New page. To check your version, open the Apple menu, choose About This Mac, and read the macOS version.

faq.question: Does Keynote for iCloud work on a second display too?
faq.answer: Yes, but the steps differ from the Mac app. Click Play in the toolbar, open the presenter display from the bottom center, drag the slideshow window to the connected display, then click Full Screen.

faq.question: Can I play the slideshow without the presenter display?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose Play > In Window, then use Play > Hide Presenter Display in Window if you do not want the presenter view on your Mac.

faq.question: How do I stop the slideshow?
faq.answer: Press Esc to stop the slideshow. Practice this once before the talk so you do not search for the key on stage.

faq.question: Why don't my speaker notes appear on the presenter display?
faq.answer: Open Display Configuration from the presenter display toolbar and check that Presenter Notes is turned on. You can also show or hide the current slide, next slide, clock, and timer in the same place.

task: Play a Keynote slideshow on a second display
appliesTo: Keynote 15.4 for Mac on macOS 26 or later, with one external display
requirements: A Mac on macOS 26 or later for Keynote 15.4
An external display or projector connected by cable or adapter
Your presentation open in Keynote for Mac
Display mirroring turned off in System Settings > Displays

steps.name: Connect the external display
steps.text: Connect the display with a cable or adapter, then switch it on. Wait until macOS detects it before you open the presentation.
steps.tip: Test the exact cable you plan to bring to the event.

steps.name: Turn off mirroring
steps.text: Open System Settings from the Apple menu, then go to Displays. Under Arrange, make sure the thumbnails are not stacked. If they are, hold Option and drag the topmost display to either side.
steps.tip: Mirroring copies your Mac screen, so the presenter display has nowhere to go.

steps.name: Open the presentation and pick the starting slide
steps.text: Open your deck in Keynote on your Mac. In the slide navigator, click the slide where you want to start. The slideshow begins on the slide you select.
steps.tip: Check the slide before you press Play, not after.

steps.name: Choose In Fullscreen
steps.text: Click Play in the menu bar, then choose In Fullscreen. This runs the show full screen, which is the mode that sends the slideshow to the external display.
steps.tip: In Window is in the same menu if you need your desktop visible.

steps.name: Click the Play button in the toolbar
steps.text: Click the Play button in the toolbar. The slideshow moves to the external display, and the presenter display stays on your Mac.
steps.tip: If nothing moves, return to System Settings > Displays and check mirroring again.

steps.name: Check which screen shows what
steps.text: Look at both screens. The external display should show the slide only. Your Mac should show the presenter display with the current slide, the next slide, and your notes.
steps.tip: If the screens are swapped, use the X key in the next step.

steps.name: Swap screens with X if needed
steps.text: Press X to swap which display shows the slideshow and which shows the presenter display. Keep pressing X until the audience sees the slide.
steps.tip: Swapping does not change your slides or your notes.

steps.name: Open the presenter display tools
steps.text: Move the pointer anywhere on the presenter display, then click a button at the top to show the toolbar. Choose Display Configuration at the top right to show or hide the current slide, next slide, presenter notes, clock, or timer.
steps.tip: Hide anything you do not read. A simpler screen is easier to glance at.

steps.name: Stop the slideshow
steps.text: When you finish, press Esc to stop the slideshow. Practice this key once so you do not hunt for it on stage.
steps.tip: Keep Esc in mind if the audience screen freezes.

troubleshooting.problem: The presenter display does not appear on my Mac
troubleshooting.fix: Turn off mirroring in System Settings > Displays and make sure the thumbnails under Arrange are not stacked. Then play again in full screen.

troubleshooting.problem: The slideshow is on the wrong screen
troubleshooting.fix: Press X until the slideshow is on the audience screen. For more control, open Display Configuration, click Configure on the thumbnail, choose Show Slideshow, then click Done.

troubleshooting.problem: My laptop screen goes black in full screen over HDMI
troubleshooting.fix: An Apple Community thread on macOS 13.5 reported this, and Apple did not reply. Test your cable and adapter before the event, and use Play > In Window as a fallback.

troubleshooting.problem: Keynote > Settings > Slideshow has no presenter display option
troubleshooting.fix: Apple's current list shows Show presenter display in other applications, with no Presenter Display checkbox for full screen. Do not rely on a checkbox from an older thread. Use Display Configuration instead.

troubleshooting.problem: Viewers can see the presenter window
troubleshooting.fix: Turn off mirroring. Apple says that without this setting, viewers may see the presenter window in Keynote for iCloud.
Open Display Configuration and turn on Presenter Notes. Then check that the notes were typed into the slide before the talk.
